newsitem.title: BELGIUM: U.S. vows no NATO nuclear weapons in east.
newsitem.headline: U.S. vows no NATO nuclear weapons in east.

text.p: The United States said on Tuesday NATO would not station nuclear weapons on the territory of new members it plans to admit from central and eastern Europe.

"In today's Europe NATO has no intention, no plan and no need to station nuclear weapons on the terriory of any new members," U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher said at the start of a two-day meeting of alliance foreign ministers.

The focus of Tuesday's meeting was to set a summit, which officials said was almost certain to be held on July 8-9 next year at a location yet to be decided, to identify and plan for new members from ex-communist eastern Europe.

"Today we convene a NATO summit for July of next year, which will shape the new NATO -- a NATO with new structures, new missions and ultimately with new members," NATO Secretary General Javier Solana told the opening session of the meeting.
"Next year's summit will mark the moment when the processes of transformation and change converge and the new Alliance takes stock," he said.

Tuesday's meeting will also discuss what to offer eastern hopefuls who are thought unlikely to be in the first enlargement wave -- notably the Baltic States, Romania and Slovakia -- and how to sweeten the expansion for a deeply opposed Russia.
In a clear attempt to assuage Russia, which resolutely opposes NATO's expansion plans, Christopher also emphasised that "no NATO nuclear forces are presently on alert".
NATO intends to invite a handful of former communist foes to begin accession talks at the special summit of NATO leaders.
Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic are currently the favourites to be invited first from a list of 11 hopefuls.
Spanish Foreign Minister Abel Matutes said on arrival the summit would probably be held on July 8-9, but said he did not yet know where. Spain has offered Madrid as a possible location.
